edges.reason: setDelay requires msg.sender == address(this), gating the delay update.
acceptAdmin requires msg.sender == pendingAdmin before transferring the admin role.
setPendingAdmin requires msg.sender == address(this) before nominating a pending admin.
queueTransaction requires msg.sender == admin before queueing.
cancelTransaction requires msg.sender == admin before cancelling.
executeTransaction requires msg.sender == admin before executing.
acceptAdmin assigns msg.sender to the admin state variable.
acceptAdmin reads pendingAdmin to authorize the caller and then clears it.
queueTransaction reads admin to authorize the caller.
cancelTransaction reads admin to authorize the caller.
executeTransaction reads admin to authorize the caller.
getBlockTimestamp returns block.timestamp, a miner-influenced value used for timelock checks.
queueTransaction uses getBlockTimestamp().add(delay) to validate eta.
executeTransaction compares getBlockTimestamp() against eta and eta.add(GRACE_PERIOD).
queueTransaction requires eta >= block.timestamp + delay, reading the delay state variable.
setDelay writes the delay_ argument into the delay state variable.
queueTransaction writes true into queuedTransactions[txHash].
cancelTransaction writes false into queuedTransactions[txHash].
executeTransaction reads and clears queuedTransactions[txHash].
executeTransaction requires block.timestamp <= eta + GRACE_PERIOD to reject stale transactions.
constructor validates _delay against MINIMUM_DELAY.
setDelay validates delay_ against MINIMUM_DELAY.
constructor validates _delay against MAXIMUM_DELAY.
setDelay validates delay_ against MAXIMUM_DELAY.
constructor writes the initial privileged admin address.
constructor writes the initial delay value.
_admin constructor parameter flows into the admin state variable.
_delay constructor parameter flows into the delay state variable.
constructor and delay bound checks rely on SafeMath helpers for arithmetic safety.
delay_ parameter is range-checked and assigned to delay in setDelay.
pendingAdmin_ parameter is assigned to the pendingAdmin state variable.
target parameter is abi.encode'd into txHash in queueTransaction.
value parameter is abi.encode'd into txHash in queueTransaction.
signature parameter is abi.encode'd into txHash in queueTransaction.
data parameter is abi.encode'd into txHash in queueTransaction.
eta parameter is abi.encode'd into txHash and checked against the delay.
target parameter is abi.encode'd into txHash in cancelTransaction.
value parameter is abi.encode'd into txHash in cancelTransaction.
signature parameter is abi.encode'd into txHash in cancelTransaction.
data parameter is abi.encode'd into txHash in cancelTransaction.
eta parameter is abi.encode'd into txHash in cancelTransaction.
target parameter is abi.encode'd into txHash in executeTransaction.
value parameter is abi.encode'd into txHash in executeTransaction.
signature parameter is used to build callData and txHash in executeTransaction.
data parameter is used to build callData and txHash in executeTransaction.
eta parameter is compared against block.timestamp and abi.encode'd into txHash.
target parameter becomes the callee address of the low-level call.
value parameter becomes the ether amount forwarded by the low-level call.
callData local variable is the argument passed to the low-level call.
txHash computed in queueTransaction is used to set queuedTransactions[txHash] = true.
txHash computed in cancelTransaction is used to set queuedTransactions[txHash] = false.
txHash computed in executeTransaction is used to read and clear the queued flag.
executeTransaction performs an external low-level call before emitting the final event.
The low-level call can invoke an attacker-controlled contract that reenters executeTransaction or other timelock functions.
The low-level call returns the success flag checked by the require afterwards.
The low-level call returns returnData which is returned to the caller.
queueTransaction uses SafeMath add for block.timestamp + delay.
executeTransaction uses SafeMath add for eta + GRACE_PERIOD.
Timelock self-calls (e.g. acceptAdmin) are delivered through executeTransaction's low-level call.
setPendingAdmin can be invoked as a self-call executed through executeTransaction.
setDelay can be invoked as a self-call executed through executeTransaction.
